observed_weakness: The scalar SFMO smoke used 648 NFE for only 48 nominal grazing trials, and the protected MO-SFMO repeats up to 20 grazing batches plus migration batches before switching state; its 2000-NFE diagnostic ZDT1 normalized HV was zero.
suspected_mechanism: Sequentially executing multiple costly behaviors for every sheep consumes most of the fixed NFE before population-level environmental feedback can change behavior, while repeated migration can amplify the imbalance unpredictably.
proposed_modification: For every active sheep and generation, select exactly one of grazing, collective migration, or regrouping from its stagnation state; generate and evaluate exactly one offspring, then perform one population/archive update. Retain N=100, fixed baseline step schedules, external archive, constraints, and no success-history adaptation.
expected_effects: At least 10 percent lower runtime or time-to-95-HV than the initial incumbent at equal NFE
More environmental-selection cycles and higher normalized-HV AUC
No mean final normalized-HV loss greater than 0.005 after intermediate evidence
possible_downsides: Shallower local exploitation can reduce final precision
One-shot switching probabilities can overuse migration on multimodal problems
More frequent archive sorting may consume some of the saved runtime
novelty: Controlled replacement of SFMO's sequential multi-behavior cycle by an energy-budgeted individual one-shot state decision, expressed as sheep grazing/migration/regrouping rather than a generic operator mixture.
falsification_evidence: Quick runtime improvement below 10 percent without at least 1 percent normalized-HV/AUC gain
Any development-instance final normalized-HV loss above 0.02
Intermediate mean normalized-HV loss above 0.005 or IGD+ regression above 5 percent without compensating locked efficiency acceptance
